unit: T3 Unit D — the funding letter pack produces nothing
whatChanged: When the letter pack comes back with no letters in it, it now says why. Before, every empty pack said the same two words — "empty pack" — whether the credit file was broken, missing, or the client simply had nothing to dispute. Now there are four different answers: no credit pull on file yet, the scoring engine broke (with the actual error text), the engine ran fine and there was nothing to send, or no engine result was handed in at all. Nothing was invented and no letter text changed — a pack that has nothing still returns nothing, it just explains itself.

notes: VERDICT ON THE CORRECTION — the audit finding is REFUTED, your grounding pass was right. src/underwrite/funding-letter-pdf.mjs renders no PDF and never did. Its two functions are persistFundingLetterFiles (writes already-made PDFs into the documents registry) and loadFundingLetterPdf (reads one back). Its own header line 1 says so: 'Persist + load funding-stack PDFs'. The only rendering in this area is renderAllPDFs, imported from the vendored ./vendor/render-pdf.cjs by letter-pack.mjs:9. The audit named the wrong function. I left funding-letter-pdf.mjs untouched.

REAL CAUSE, PROVEN, NOT ASSUMED. I ran the actual demo payload through the actual function. buildSimulatedCrsPayload() has no `bureaus` key -> rawResponsesFromMerged finds zero bureau reports and throws at src/finance/crs-tier.mjs:37 -> buildLetterPackForClient catches it into engineSkip and leaves the engine null -> zero files -> reason 'empty_pack'. Observed output before my change: {files: 0, reason: 'empty_pack', engineSkip: 'rawResponsesFromMerged: no bureau reports to score'}. After my change the same run reports reason: 'engine_error: rawResponsesFromMerged: no bureau reports to score'.

PROOF THE REST OF THE PACK IS HEALTHY. I fed a real merged bureau payload (the vendored CRS sandbox TU/EX/EQ reports) through buildLetterPackForClient with a fake database. It produced 7 real PDFs: inquiry_ex, inquiry_eq, personal_info_ex, personal_info_tu, personal_info_eq, ex_round1, eq_round1, engine tier MANUAL_REVIEW, engineSkip null. So there is no second bug hiding inside my files. This is now pinned as a test.

LOUD — I CHANGED AN EXISTING TEST. src/underwrite/letter-pack.test.mjs had a test asserting pack.reason === 'empty_pack' when no engine result was supplied. That test was asserting the exact conflation you asked me to fix, so it could not stay. It is now named 'no engine result reports no_engine_result, not a bare empty_pack' and asserts the new value plus assert.notEqual against 'empty_pack'. I weakened nothing and deleted nothing else. I also added a comment above it dated 2026-08-19 saying why it changed, so the next reader does not think it drifted.

THE FOUR STATES ARE NOW DISTINGUISHABLE. Verified by running all four: no crs row -> 'no_crs_result'; stored pull missing result.bureaus -> 'engine_error: rawResponsesFromMerged: no bureau reports to score'; engine throws -> 'engine_error: <message>'; engine ran clean and found nothing -> 'empty_pack'. 'no_crs_result' is deliberately NOT called an engine error — a client with no credit pull yet is a normal early state, not a fault.

WHY THE REASON STRING AND NOT A NEW FIELD. Both callers collapse the failure down to one string: src/workflows/c-06-crs-results-router.mjs:93 and src/workflows/ds-02-diy-letters.mjs:65 both read `pack.reason || pack.engineSkip`. A non-null reason always wins, and ds-02's failure branch drops engineSkip entirely. Any new field would have been thrown away before a human saw it. So the detail had to go into `reason` itself. I did not edit either caller — they pick the new values up unchanged.

TESTS ADDED (5 new): engine result that yields nothing still reports the benign empty_pack; a stored pull WITH result.bureaus builds real letters through the tier engine (end to end, real engine, asserts %PDF headers); a stored pull WITHOUT result.bureaus names the engine fault, not empty_pack; an engine that throws is reported as engine_error with its message; and in crs-tier.test.mjs, a stored pull with flat tradelines but no bureaus key still throws — that last one pins the exact demo-seed shape, which looks like a complete payload and is why it went unnoticed.

ONE EXTRA SILENT SWALLOW CLOSED, SAME FUNCTION. The summary-document block in buildLetterPack had a bare `catch { summaries = []; }` that threw the error away — the identical bug, ten lines from the one you sent me after. It now records the message on a new `summarySkip` field, matching the existing `deliverableSkip` idiom. Purely additive, changes no reason value and no behaviour. Flagging it because it is one step past the literal task.

COMPLIANCE: nothing to flag. No letter wording changed, no customer-facing text touched, no claim about credit outcomes written or altered. Every change is to internal status strings that only staff and logs see. No letter is invented, no bureau is fabricated, and an empty pack is still empty — it just explains itself now.

OWNED BUT NOT TOUCHED, ON PURPOSE: src/underwrite/funding-letter-pdf.mjs (the audit was wrong about it), src/underwrite/letter-pack-filter.mjs (pure filtering, correct as written), src/underwrite/report.mjs (unrelated — it is the UnderwriteIQ Lite report assembler, nothing to do with the letter pack).

LEFT UNDONE, DELIBERATE — one more illegible reason I did not chase. 'missing_funding_analysis' has the same weakness: in my sandbox run the true cause was simply that ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not set, which sits in `deliverableSkip` and gets dropped by the callers. I left it alone because that pack is NOT empty (it delivers 7 letters, so c-06 never reads the reason at all) and fixing it is outside this unit. Worth a separate small task if you want it.
